## How much does it cost to rent an H100 or H200?

A comparison updated October 1, 2026 by Thunder Compute, itself a GPU cloud, lists on-demand H100 prices from $2.99 per GPU-hour at Vultr and $3.29 at Lambda to $6.88 at AWS, $6.98 at Azure and $10.98 at Google Cloud. results.title: Recompute Token Cost Before Q4 GPU Reservations — The Serving Desk
results.author: 3 MIN
highlights:
GPU reservations trade committed capacity for a fixed rate, but a fixed rate can become a stale rate when on-demand prices move. The arithmetic is simple: cost per token equals the GPU-hour rate divided by tokens per GPU-hour, so the percentage change in rate becomes the percentage change in token cost when throughput holds. Nebius, an AI cloud provider, is repricing its Nvidia GPU fleet on October 1, the second on-demand reset in three months.

The H100 moves from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, a 16.9% increase. H200 and B200 rates move to $5.40 and $8.50 per GPU-hour, increases of 20% and 18.9%. The B300 jumps from $7.85 to $9.50 on October 1, a 21% increase.

On 5 June 2025, AWS cut its H100 on-demand price by 44% in a single announcement. That is not a gradual drift. It is nearly half the price, overnight, from the largest cloud provider in the world.

Other providers did not wait long. Through June and July 2025, several cut their own prices by 20% to 25%, again in single moves rather than small steps.

...

## Late 2025 into 2026: the reversal

Then the direction flipped.

- Contract prices rose about 40%. SemiAnalysis tracked one-year H100 contracts rising from $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour between October 2025 and March 2026.
- The rental index jumped 10% in four weeks. Silicon Data's H100 rental index went from $2.00 to $2.20 between December 2025 and January 2026.

results.title: GPU Rental Prices Fall 11% in September Despite Median ...
results.author: GPU Economy
highlights: The median price of an H100 GPU-hour fell 11% in September. Prices didn't. Our weekly median of listed on-demand H100 SXM rates went from $3.92 (week of Sep 7) to $3.49 (week of Sep 28). A headline writes itself: GPU rental prices are falling. Except they weren't. Over the same weeks our like-for-like index, which compares each cloud only with its own earlier price, ended the month at 100.8: up 0.8%, not down. What moved the median was the panel. We read 18 providers' H100 rates in the first week and 29 in the last, and the clouds that joined list below the ones already there. A median over a growing panel falls when cheaper sellers arrive, even if nobody cuts a price. Two more figures from the month: - monthly average: $3.88 per H100 GPU-hour, over 589 hourly readings - the four hyperscalers held at $9.90 all month; specialist GPU clouds ended at $3.20, 3.1 times less If you quote GPU prices, quote the index and the panel size with the median. Every figure links to the provider page it was read from, the weekly receipts list every quote, and the data is free under CC BY 4.0. September report (2 pages, PDF) and the frozen month: https://lnkd.in/eXe8EYxd #GPU #AIInfrastructure #CloudComputing #H100 #ComputePrices

results.title: Affordable compute is becoming a condition for using AI. How ...
highlights:
- Older GPUs are getting cheaper, the newest are not. The AIMultiple Cloud GPU Price Index, which tracks 75 providers, puts the September 2026 on-demand median at $3.25 per hour for an H100 and $4.40 for an H200, while a B200 sits at $6.52. The median for the newest generation of chips has more than doubled since October 2024, from $2.12 to $4.72 per hour.
- The same chip can cost six times more depending on who sells it. In the same index, an H200 hour ranges from about $2 to almost $14. Where you buy matters as much as what you buy.
- The giants are spending at a scale no one else can match. Analyst tallies of company guidance put 2026 capital expenditure by Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta above $700 billion combined. Most of the newest capacity is committed to them and their largest customers.
- Power is the next constraint. The International Energy Agency expects electricity use by data centres to more than double by 2030. New capacity now waits on grid connections, not only on chips.
- The price of a token keeps falling, the bill does not. The Ramp AI Index reports that the average price US businesses pay per million tokens fell 41% between March and September 2026. Usage grows faster than prices fall, especially once agents start running multi-step tasks on their own.
